message: In the under-deck vertical Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) at midspan (C1), the tuning to the 1.9 Hertz (Hz) mode and added damping ratio has needed off-tune proof, Manager and Structural Dynamics Lead. To check it I used Den Hartog optimisation reusing the optimal TMD sizing (E4) with the detuned damping estimate (E8) and the off-tune check (E13). I found 400 kilograms at 1.86 Hz with 0.086 TMD damping ratio holding 0.064 effective damping and 0.136 metres per second squared at plus 5 percent detune, according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose retaining two 200 kilogram modules with slotted spring seats for re-tuning. My position: ready because tuning and damping survive detune. In the under-deck vertical Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) retrofit (C1), the crowd-walking comfort reduction without changing deck appearance has needed final proof, Manager. To check it I used resonant comparison reusing the resonant response calculation (E1) with the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6). I found about 0.20 metres per second squared controlled versus 1.75 metres per second squared baseline with about 8.2 millimetres stroke within 30 millimetres clearance, according to Human Induced Vibrations of Steel Structures, 2008. I propose holding concealed midspan placement accessed from below. My position: ready because comfort and stroke margin are closed.
